title: P22A1 — the secret-file argv boundary for the deploy artifact
problem: A deploy artifact needs a real database credential, but every ordinary way of handing one over leaks it: a command-line argument is visible to any process that can read the process table, an environment variable is inherited by every child and dumped by most crash reporters, and a baked-in value becomes an immutable image layer. Nothing in this repository yet defines how the credential crosses that boundary, so P22 could not start without first fixing the argument shape.
solution: One small wrapper, host/deploy/secret_file_runner.mjs, accepts exactly two mounted FILE PATHS (--config-file and --database-url-file), reads and validates both fail-closed, rewrites only its own in-process JS process.argv into the argument contract the existing host/js_asgi runner already owns, and then delegates to that runner by dynamic import. The credential value therefore never appears as an OS argument, never comes from the environment, and is never composed by a second, unaudited code path.

acceptanceScenarios.title: the wrapper takes only mounted file paths and delegates to the existing runner
acceptanceScenarios.asserts: Both closed flags exist; no environment read; no shell or process-spawning fallback; no direct reimplementation of the boundary composition; the existing ../js_asgi/create_customer_asgi_runner.mjs is reached through a dynamic import performed only after the mounts validate; the validated values are handed over through this process's own process.argv and through nothing else; policy=allow, audit=on, trustedTenantId and trustedActorId are each validated before delegation.

acceptanceScenarios.title: every bad mount fails closed without disclosing the credential, and a good pair reaches the existing runner
acceptanceScenarios.asserts: An absent, unreadable, empty or malformed mount exits non-zero, names the path but never the contents, and never attempts PostgreSQL contact; an inline credential argument is refused as an unrecognized argument without being echoed; a config carrying a non-allow policy, a non-on audit, a nil trusted tenant or a non-visible-ASCII trusted actor is refused; with both mounts complete the live child blocks on stdin, its OS-visible argv as ps reports it carries only the two mounted PATHS, and a malformed stdin envelope is refused by the EXISTING runner's own message, proving delegation actually happened.

acceptanceScenarios.title: the planning manifest binds this package to its base, allowed paths, split evidence, rollback and unchanged readiness
acceptanceScenarios.asserts: This manifest records the immutable base commit and tree, the canonical Actionplan change-package budget pin, the frozen test path and its recomputed sha256, the exact targeted command, the frozen scope and parent scope hashes, the rejected combined-test hash and its exact rejection reason, the outstanding P22A2/P22B/P22C remainder, the 21/25 counter, one-writer provenance, the rollback mechanism and blast radius, measured Git metrics over exactly three files inside the class ceiling, the unchanged readiness flag set, the declared non-goals, the fixed capability-delta prefix, both product claims and the five Turkish owner-facing fields.

conditionalDeliveryGates.evidence: One problem only: how a mounted credential reaches the existing runner without becoming an OS argument. No container, no listener, no database, no registry, no roadmap edit.
Exactly three files, declared in allowedFiles before the first write and unchanged since: this manifest, the frozen test and the one new wrapper. No existing file is touched.

The wrapper reimplements no argument parsing, no identity construction and no boundary composition; it validates its own two mounts and delegates the rest to the runner that already owns that contract.

Every failure path is fail-closed and non-disclosing, the trusted-identity forms match the ones the existing runner enforces, and the honest limit of an in-process argv rewrite is written down in the wrapper rather than overclaimed.
Targeted RED-to-GREEN is the writer's; one full local QA run is the writer's single budgeted execution and the CI full run is the second. Recorded by the reviewer, not asserted here.
A separate read-only session on this immutable snapshot must accept the package. The writer cannot review the package the writer wrote, and any change to the snapshot invalidates the review.
Deleting the two added files returns the tree to base b3af22aa0b606fad3fad0e2267176e8d00ba13df. Nothing was deployed, so nothing has to be undone anywhere else.

rollback.mechanism: Delete host/deploy/secret_file_runner.mjs and planning/kernel-deploy-secret-boundary-p22a1.json (and the frozen test if the whole package is withdrawn). No existing file was modified, so removal alone restores the base tree exactly.
rollback.blastRadius: Confined to two new files plus the frozen test. No src module, no existing host module, no schema, no migration, no dependency, no CI workflow and no running system is touched, so removal cannot regress anything that worked before.
rollback.compensatingStepReason: The wrapper was never deployed, never started a listener, never contacted a database and never pushed an image, so there is no external effect to compensate for.

nonGoals: No container image and no OCI build of any kind: the container is P22A2's, not this package's.
No network listener is started, bound or selected here; no HTTP server is imported.
No deployment, promotion, staging run or external environment change is performed or implied.
No database connection is opened and no PostgreSQL instance is contacted; the credential is validated as text and handed on, never used.
No registry is contacted, authenticated against or pushed to.
No roadmap document is edited and no phase counter is advanced.
No current-truth closure is written; P22C alone closes P22 in the roadmap current truth.
No existing runner, composition, schema, dependency or CI workflow is modified.
No production host is selected for the deploy artifact and no readiness flag beyond the declared set is introduced.
capabilityDelta: SECRET_FILE_ARGV_BOUNDARY: a deploy artifact can now be handed its database credential as a mounted file path instead of an inline argument — the wrapper validates the mounted config and database-url files fail-closed, rewrites only its own in-process JS process.argv, and delegates to the existing audited host runner, so the credential value is never an OS-visible argument, never read from the environment and never disclosed by a refusal. This is an argument-shape boundary only; it starts nothing and deploys nothing.

productClaim.runnable: The wrapper runs today under `node host/deploy/secret_file_runner.mjs --config-file <path> --database-url-file <path>`: it validates both mounts, refuses every absent, unreadable, empty, malformed or non-conforming mount without echoing the credential, and on a valid pair reaches the existing audited runner, which then waits for its stdin envelope exactly as it already did.
productClaim.notRunnable: There is still no runnable product. Nothing here builds an image, starts a listener, provisions an environment, contacts PostgreSQL or serves a single real HTTP request. A user cannot submit a form, save a record or see an audit row as a result of this package; that needs P22A2, P22B and P22C, and readiness beyond runtimeImplementationStarted stays false.

userJourney.once: Önceden, bir CRM formundan gelen kaydın veritabanına ulaşabilmesi için veritabanı parolasının ya komut satırına yazılması ya da ortam değişkenine konması gerekiyordu; her iki yol da parolayı makinedeki başka süreçlere ve çökme kayıtlarına açıyordu, bu yüzden gerçek bir sunucuya kurulum hiç denenemiyordu.
userJourney.simdi: Şimdi kurulumu yapan taraf parolayı bir dosyaya koyup sadece o dosyanın yolunu veriyor. Program dosyayı kendisi okuyor, içeriğini hiçbir hata mesajında göstermiyor, eksik ya da bozuk dosyada hemen duruyor ve doğruysa mevcut denetimli çalıştırıcıya devrediyor.
userJourney.fark: Fark, parolanın artık işletim sisteminin süreç listesinde görünmemesi. Aynı makinedeki başka bir program `ps` ile baksa yalnızca dosya yolunu görür, parolanın kendisini göremez; ayrıca ikinci bir gizli okuma yolu (ortam değişkeni veya kabuk çağrısı) bilerek hiç bırakılmadı.
userJourney.kullaniciYolculugu: Bir CRM kullanıcısı müşteri formunu doldurup kaydet dediğinde isteğin veritabanına gidebilmesi için sistemin parolayı bilmesi gerekir. Bu paket o parolanın sisteme güvenli biçimde girmesini çözüyor; ancak formun kendisi hâlâ çalışmıyor, çünkü ortada ne çalışan bir sunucu ne de bağlanılan bir veritabanı var.
userJourney.kalanEngel: Kalan engel üç adım: P22A2 taşınabilir imajı üretecek, P22B geçici PostgreSQL 16 ortamında gerçek HTTP isteğini ve denetim kaydını kanıtlayacak, P22C ise yol haritasındaki güncel gerçeği kapatacak. Bunlar bitmeden hiçbir gerçek kullanıcı hiçbir formu kaydedemez.

residualRisks: An in-process process.argv rewrite cannot change the OS command line already recorded for this pid. The wrapper says so explicitly and the frozen test asserts only the narrower true claim — that the credential VALUE is never an OS argument — so the boundary must not later be described as hiding an argument that was already there.

The credential still lives in a file on the host filesystem. This package fixes the argument shape only; mount permissions, secret rotation and the storage backing that mount stay outside it and remain a deployment-time responsibility.

Once the mounted pair validates, the credential is held in this process's memory and in its rewritten process.argv, so a core dump or an in-process debugger of this same process could still observe it. That exposure is inherent to any process that must use a credential and is not claimed to be solved.

Delegation is proven here only as far as the existing runner's own malformed-envelope refusal. That the runner then connects, writes and audits correctly against a real database is P22B's proof and is not asserted by this package.

The wrapper's config contract is deliberately closed and exact. A future deploy configuration that legitimately needs another field will fail closed until the contract and its frozen test are extended in a separate package, which is the intended trade.
